findings.fix: The stone lands at (x, y) = (2v₀²tanθ/g, −2v₀²tan²θ/g); the negative sign shows the landing point lies below the launch point, as in the figure.

findings.quote: Set up coordinates at the launch point, with x horizontal along v₀ and y taken positive down the slope's vertical direction; write x and y as functions of time.
findings.note: The question already gives the axes (origin at the throw point, y vertical, negative below the origin); this step overrides them with y positive downward, and the phrase "down the slope's vertical direction" is not a clear statement of any convention.
findings.fix: Use the axes given in the question: origin at the launch point, x horizontal along v₀, y vertical and positive upward. Then x(t) = v₀t and y(t) = −½gt².

notes: My independent solve: x = v₀t, y = −½gt², hill line y = −x tanθ, so t = 2v₀tanθ/g, x = 2v₀²tanθ/g, y = −2v₀²tan²θ/g.
